ON.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
ON.name: Community Legal Clinics (Legal Aid Ontario)
ON.summary: Legal clinics funded by Legal Aid Ontario give legal information, advice or representation. Enter your postal code in the clinic finder.

ON.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
ON.name: ARCH Disability Law Centre
ON.summary: A specialty legal clinic that practises only disability rights law and serves people with disabilities who have low income in Ontario.

ON.name: 211 Ontario
ON.summary: A helpline and website linking people to social services, programs and community supports.

ON.name: Disability Alliance Canada
ON.summary: A national organization that says it serves people with disabilities across Canada. Offers free advocate support through CPP Disability and the Disability Tax Credit (DTC).

ON.name: Disability Planning Helpline (Plan Institute)
ON.summary: A free, nationwide (Canada-wide) helpline for disability planning questions, including the RDSP.

SK.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
SK.name: Pro Bono Law Saskatchewan
SK.summary: Runs free legal clinics across Saskatchewan and a Panel Program that matches clients with volunteer lawyers.

SK.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
SK.name: CLASSIC (Saskatoon)
SK.summary: Provides free legal programming, services and supports for people who experience poverty and injustice in Saskatoon.

SK.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
SK.name: Saskatchewan Human Rights Commission
SK.summary: Works to discourage and eliminate discrimination; has a Duty to Accommodate page and accommodation resources.

SK.name: 211 Saskatchewan
SK.summary: Free, confidential information on health and social services by phone, text or chat, live answer 24/7.

SK.name: Disability Alliance Canada
SK.summary: A national organization that says it serves people with disabilities across Canada. Offers free advocate support through CPP Disability and the Disability Tax Credit (DTC).

MB.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
MB.name: Legal Aid Manitoba
MB.summary: Free or affordable legal services for low-income adults and youth. Covers government benefit appeals (social assistance, CPP disability, Workers Compensation) and some human rights cases; decided case by case, with financial eligibility rules.

MB.cat: If you're denied — legal help & appeals
MB.name: Manitoba Human Rights Commission
MB.summary: Administers The Human Rights Code, which prohibits disability discrimination in employment, services available to the public, contracts and housing. An Aug 21, 2026 notice on the site said phones were down; email hrc@gov.mb.ca with your name and phone number.

MB.name: 211 Manitoba
MB.summary: Free, confidential information on health and social services by phone, live answer 24/7, plus online and chat.

MB.name: Disability Alliance Canada
MB.summary: A national organization that says it serves people with disabilities across Canada. Offers free advocate support through CPP Disability and the Disability Tax Credit (DTC).

MB.name: Disability Planning Helpline (Plan Institute)
MB.summary: A free, nationwide (Canada-wide) helpline for disability planning questions, including the RDSP.

SK.name: SaskAbilities
SK.whatTheyDo: Offers independent living, community, supported employment and other programs and services for people with disabilities.

SK.name: Inclusion Saskatchewan
SK.whatTheyDo: Supports people with intellectual disabilities, their families and community groups, working with government and partners to expand inclusion and choice.

SK.name: Spinal Cord Injury Saskatchewan
SK.whatTheyDo: Supports people with spinal cord injuries and other physical disabilities, and their families, to live independently and take part in community life.

SK.name: Saskatchewan Deaf and Hard of Hearing Services
SK.whatTheyDo: Provides services for Deaf and hard of hearing people, including ASL interpreting, family and vocational support, note-taking and assistive devices.

SK.name: Autism Resource Centre
SK.whatTheyDo: Uses education and skill-building services to help autistic people grow their abilities and engage with their community.

MB.name: Manitoba Possible
MB.region: Brandon, Dauphin, Morden, Selkirk, Steinbach, Thompson, Winnipeg
MB.whatTheyDo: Runs programs and services for Manitobans with disabilities, their families and communities, working to eliminate barriers to full and equal participation.

MB.name: Abilities Manitoba
MB.whatTheyDo: A network of agencies supporting people with intellectual disabilities, offering advocacy, training, employment resources and e-learning.

MB.name: Inclusion Winnipeg
MB.whatTheyDo: Supports people who face barriers to services and advocates for equal citizenship and inclusive communities.
